question: Should ClawHub track and support failures from the legacy `molt.bot` zsh-piped installer, or should that path be retired/redirected to the current supported OpenClaw and ClawHub install commands?
rationale: The reported helper is absent from current main, while the live URL redirects to a hosted installer outside this repository, so automation cannot safely choose the ownership or support boundary.

options.title: Retire or redirect legacy zsh usage
options.body: Point users to the current `openclaw.ai` bash installer and maintained OpenClaw/ClawHub install commands, then treat the legacy zsh-piped `molt.bot` cleanup failure as unsupported.

options.title: Own and harden the hosted installer
options.body: Track the hosted installer source, reproduce the Homebrew/zsh cleanup failure, and fix unmatched npm cleanup globs with validation for supported shells and Node versions.

options.title: Wait for current reporter proof
options.body: Keep this waiting on author until there is fresh evidence that a currently supported install path still fails.

recommendation.title: Retire or redirect legacy zsh usage
recommendation.body: Point users to the current `openclaw.ai` bash installer and maintained OpenClaw/ClawHub install commands, then treat the legacy zsh-piped `molt.bot` cleanup failure as unsupported.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen is the strongest visible routing candidate for the current ClawHub CLI/package install surface and has already triaged this issue.
